title: Maize and Cereal Common Rust Management Manual
snippet: # Year: 2026 ## Disease Characteristics Common rust of maize is caused by the obligate biotrophic fungus Puccinia sorghi. The fungus produces small, circular-to-elongate golden-brown to cinnamon-brown powdery pustules (uredinia) scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces. ## Environmental Drivers Puccinia sorghi proliferates under moderate temperatures (16°C–25°C) combined with high relative humidity and dew durations exceeding 6 hours.

title: Tomato Early Blight Management & Prevention Guide
snippet: # Year: 2026 ## Overview of Alternaria Solani Early blight, caused by the fungal pathogen Alternaria solani, affects tomato and potato crops worldwide. The fungus produces characteristic concentric brown circular lesions on lower leaves, resembling target rings or a bullseye pattern. Yellow chlorotic margins typically surround the dark necrotic centers. ## Optimal Growth Conditions The disease progresses rapidly when foliage remains wet for exten

title: Tomato Early Blight Management & Prevention Guide
